newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE wheat edges up, short-term floor seen.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE wheat edges up, short-term floor seen.

text.p: Australian wheat futures rose slightly again on Friday as the market seemed to find its short-term floor, dealers said.
May 1997 rose by A$1.50 to A$151.00 a tonne on four trades while July 1997 edged up by 50 cents to A$152.50, also on four trades. Two A$135.00 January 1997 put options also traded at A$2.50.
Gary Booth of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures Ltd said that the market was approaching or had reached a short-term low and was increasingly recognised as extremely over-sold.
Booth also noted a remarkable surge of interest in wheat futures and options by traders, hedgers and grain buyers.
Growers were concerned about lower prices but were not as concerned about buying put options because after the market's quick fall the downside was relatively limited, he said.
Booth noted that the bullish Consensus Report from the U.S. this week indicated the market was extremely oversold with only 12 percent of major traders polled bullish, he said.
"Falling volume, a fall in open interest and the bullish Consensus Report, with other technical indicators, suggest the market is approaching or making a short-term bottom," he said.
